gen-fs-array-gf-cascadia-code: Array's open-ended curves and wide lowercase eyes give it a futuristic, precisely drawn look up top. Cascadia Code follows in a wire-thin sans with generous gaps between neighbors, so a long block of text glides along without snagging.
gen-fs-array-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono reads as a compact, modern sans-serif, its capitals nearly melting into the lowercase like pins set in a wide board. And Array's open curves above it supply the one thing the body skips: a futuristic flourish.
gen-fs-array-gf-julius-sans-one: Array arrives with open-ended curves and big lowercase eyes, a futuristic voice that Julius Sans One meets with thin monoline strokes and wide gaps between letters. Display drama above, quiet spacing below.
gen-fs-array-gf-lexend-exa: Precise and futuristic, Array leads with open curves, while Lexend Exa follows in a rope-thin sans-serif with stubby ascenders and a big x-height. Give the heading plenty of size to show off those curves.
gen-fs-array-gf-lexend-giga: Crisp, futuristic, wide-eyed. Array's open-ended curves lead the way, and Lexend Giga trails behind in flat, single-weight sans-serif lines with generous tracking that lets every word breathe.
gen-fs-array-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega looks drawn with a single nib, its crossbars exactly as heavy as its stems and every c showing a visible gap. But Array is the one with flair, bending open-ended curves into something futuristic while the body simply keeps things approachable.
gen-fs-array-gf-lexend-peta: Approachable and professional, Lexend Peta has wide-mouthed c shapes, a big x-height and curves that never thin at the shoulders. Over a full page, this plain sans keeps reading easy.
gen-fs-array-gf-lexend-tera: Array brings open-ended curves and large lowercase eyes, a precise, futuristic look for the top of the page. And Lexend Tera, a plain sans drawn like a plotter pen, spaces its letters out like stepping stones beneath it.
gen-fs-array-gf-lexend-zetta: Wide-set, ribbon-cut, quietly futuristic. Lexend Zetta, a plain sans of constant stroke width with tall small letters, lets the eye skim across a long stretch of text without ever slowing down.
gen-fs-array-gf-montserrat-alternates: Montserrat Alternates reads with a c as open as a bent paperclip, round letters matching their stems, and lowercase crowding toward the capital line. Even a long page of this plain sans moves along smoothly.
